 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And
227 Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To Issue A Writ
Of Certiorari By Quashing The Impugned Intimation Letter
Dated 14.06.2021 In File No.Laq/Sr/4/2020-21/606 Issued By
The Respondent No.2 As Per Annexure- H And Issue A Writ
Of Mandamus Directing The Respondent No.2 To Proceed
With The Acquisition Proceedings In Respect Of 34 Guntas
I.E., (34 Guntas As Per Prl. Notificatiion U/Sec.11(1) And 10
Guntas Of Pot Kharab-A Land) Of Land Sy.No.128 Of Village
Araladinni Tq. Nidagundi, Dist. Vijayapura.

This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing In
'B' Group This Day

, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
a) "Issue a writ of certiorari by quashing the impugned intimation letter dated 14.06.2021 in file no.LAQ/SR/4/2020-21/606 issued by the respondent no.2 as per Annexure- H, in the interest of justice and equity.
b) Issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondent no.2 to proceed with the acquisition proceedings in respect of 34 guntas i.e., (34 guntas as per Prl. Notification U/S.11(1) and 10 guntas of pot Kharab-A land) of land sy.no.128 of village Araladinni tq.
Nidagundi, dist. Vijayapura, in the interest of justice and equity.
c) Issue any writ or order as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice and equity."

entities.text: Pandurangacharya vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner is the absolute owner of land in Sy.No.128 measuring 14 acres 16 guntas including 10 guntas of pot kharab-A situated at Araladinni village, Nidagundi Taluk, Vijayapura District.
A part of the said land measuring 13 acres 12 guntas was acquired in the year 1968 for the purpose of Almatti Dam Upper Krishna Project and compensation paid.

3. As regards, remainder 1 acre 4 guntas including 10 guntas pot kharab-A land, though said land has been utilized by the respondents, neither was the same acquired nor compensation paid.
4.

In that background, the petitioner has approached this Court in W.P.No.8262/2019 seeking for a direction to consider representation of the petitioner to acquire the land and make payment of compensation.
This Court vide order dated 06.01.2020 had directed the respondent to consider the representation of the petitioner within two months.
Subsequent thereto, the petitioner has submitted several representations.

5. It is only on 30.07.2020 that a notification under Section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short,
hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013') came to be issued that has not been proceeded with.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, an endorsement came to be issued on 14.06.2021 that since public works department has handed over possession of the entire extent of land, the said acquisition proceedings could not be proceeded with and as such in the endorsement issued by respondent No.2, Special Land Acquisition Officer (for short hereinafter referred to as 'the SLAO) on 14.06.2021 petitioner has been informed that the land would not be acquired.
It is in that background, the petitioner is before this Court.

6. Smt. Ratna N. Shivayogimath, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the land having been utilized by the respondent, the acquisition of the entire land would have to be completed or in the alternative land not acquired is to be handed over to the petitioner, which is now in the possession of the respondent.

7. Sri Shivakumar R. Tengli, learned Additional Government Advocate submits that since the possession had already been handed over long ago, the land having been already utilized, the documents available with the respondents not indicating to the contra, the endorsement which has been issued is proper and correct.
8.

Heard Smt. Ratna N. Shivayogimath, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Shivakumar R.
Tengli, learned Additional Government Advocate for respondents and perused the records.
9. It is not in dispute that the petitioner owns the land measuring 14 acres 16 guntas including 10 guntas pot kharab-A land in Sy.No.128.

It is only 13 acres 12 guntas which was acquired leaving a balance of 1 acre 4 guntas including 10 guntas pot kharab-A of Araldinni village, Nidagundi village,
Vijayapura district.
10. When such being the case, the respondents could not have used the un-acquired land for the project by creating a rock garden.

The right to property, though not a fundamental right, is a Prahallad S/O Pandurangacharya vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2998680/
3 constitutional right under Article 301 of the Constitution of India and no person can be deprived of his rights over the land without following the due process of law.

entities.text: Prahallad S/O Pandurangacharya vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In the present case, it is clear and apparent that the respondents have deprived the petitioner of 1 acre 4 guntas of his land without following due process of law.

12. The petitioner having approached this Court in W.P.No.8262/2019, and this Court having directed the respondents to consider the representation vide its order dated 06.01.2020, in furtherance of which a notification under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013 came to be issued on 30.07.2020, it was but required that the said process was to be completed for 34 guntas stated therein.
13. It is also shocking that the notification was issued only as regards 34 guntas and not balance 10 guntas claiming that the same was pot kharab-A land.

A Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Shivappa S/o Prabhappa Mugalolli vs. The General Manager, Upper Krishna Project and Another1 has held that pot kharab-A and pot kharab-B land W.P.No.106515/2015 disposed of on 07.03.2023 would enure to the benefit of the land owner entitling the land owner to compensation for both the classifications, if the same were to be acquired.

entities.text: Shivappa S/o Prabhappa Mugalolli vs. The General Manager, Upper Krishna Project and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the notification which has been issued under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013, ought to have been for the entire extent of 1 acre 4 guntas of land.

14. Be that as it may, even though, the said notification had been issued on 30.07.2020, the same was not proceeded with and the impugned endorsement has been issued by the SLAO on 14.06.2021 contending that since the PWD handed over the possession, there is no need for acquisition, the acquisition proceedings will not be proceeded with.

Such an endorsement, in my considered opinion, issued by the SLAO, would only indicate that the SLAO has no knowledge about land acquisition and or the applicable law thereto, or in the alternative the same can only be said to be malafide.

15. It is not for the SLAO to have issued the endorsement post notification having been issued for acquisition under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013 which would only amount to the SLAO negating the action of the State in exercise of the eminent domain under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013.

Role and responsibility of the SLAO post issuance of acquisition notification is only to consider the representations and or the objections which are filed and submit a report which would be acted upon by the State, the recommendations are required to be made to the State for action.
16. The SLAO by the impugned endorsement has addressed the endorsement to the petitioner stating that the acquisition cannot be completed.
The SLAO has no business to address such a correspondence to the petitioner informing about the same.

As such, I am of the considered opinion that necessary enquiry would have to be initiated for the action of the SLAO - 10 - Prahallad S/O Pandurangacharya vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2998680/
4 by the Principal Secretary, Revenue Department, which enquiry is to be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

entities.text: Prahallad S/O Pandurangacharya vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. In view of my aforesaid reasoning that the SLAO is not a proper authority to issue the endorsement dated 14.06.2021, it is but required that the same is quashed.

18. In the event of State not wishing to process the said acquisition, the only option left to the State is to handover the possession of the unacquired 1 acre 4 guntas to the petitioner so that the petitioner can make use of the said land for his benefit.

If the State were to proceed with the acquisition, it would also be required that necessary direction be issued for completion of the process pursuant to Section 11(1) notification issued under the Act of 2013.
In so far as the balance 10 guntas of land the state is at liberty - 11 - to either acquire the same or hand back the possession of that extent of land to the Petitioner.

19. As such, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed, a certiorari is issued, the intimation/ endorsement dated 14.06.2021 bearing No.LAQ/SR/04/2020-21/606 issued by the SLAO as per Annexure-H is hereby quashed.

ii. A mandamus is issued directing the respondent No.2 to proceed with the notification under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013 and complete the said process of acquisition within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of copy of this order,
failing which, the acquisition would have to be held to have lapsed.
iii. As regards, balance 10 guntas of land, if the State were not wanting to acquire the same, the possession of the same would have to be handed back to the petitioner.

If the State were wanting to acquire the said land, necessary notification to be issued as per Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013 within 4 weeks of the receipt of - 12 - a copy of this order and acquisition completed in accordance with law, in the time frame given there under.
iv.
The Principal Secretary, Revenue Department to complete the enquiry ordered above and submit a report to this Court within a period of three months from today.

Sd/-
